_description: Canonical DNOS syntax for EVPN loop-prevention (LP) and local-loop-prevention (LLP). Validated live on PE-4 (CL-86) running dev_v26_2 build 8fd38d35a10a on 2026-04-30. Every command was probed via SSH ?-walk + live execution. See scaler/TEST/_shared/tools/discover_loop_prevention*.py for the discovery scripts.

operational_show_commands.command: show evpn instance <I> loop-prevention interface local
operational_show_commands.purpose: Local-only view of the shutdown-interface table
Per-EVI MAC suppression/move table with cycles + remaining time

operational_show_commands.command: show evpn instance <I> loop-prevention mac-table local
operational_show_commands.purpose: Local-only view of the MAC suppression table

rejected_commands_with_alternatives.reason: 'local-loop-prevention' is NOT a valid show keyword (it lives only inside the config tree under mac-handling > loop-prevention)
'mac-suppression' is a CLEAR-side verb; not exposed under show evpn loop-prevention
'mac-history' is a CLEAR-side verb; show side uses mac-table for the move counters
'restore-cycles' exists ONLY as a clear verb; show side reports cycles inside mac-table column
rejected_commands_with_alternatives.use_instead: show evpn instance <I> loop-prevention mac-table  (look at the 'Cycles' column)

_clear_note: These appeared in the `clear evpn instance <I> ?` menu walk on PE-4 dev_v26_2. They are clear-side verbs only -- do NOT try them as `show` commands.

loop_prevention._purpose: Outer loop-prevention sub-tree for the entire EVI (remote MAC moves)

timer_keywords.mac-restore-timer: <seconds> -- how long a MAC stays suppressed
timer_keywords.mac-restore-max-cycles: <int> -- max suppression cycles before harder action
timer_keywords.mac-reset-restore-cycles-interval: <seconds> -- window after which the cycle counter resets

local_loop_prevention._path: network-services evpn instance <I> mac-handling loop-prevention local-loop-prevention
local_loop_prevention._purpose: Inner LLP sub-tree -- LOCAL loop detection on this EVI

timer_keywords_no_mac_prefix.restore-timer: <seconds> -- LLP equivalent of mac-restore-timer (NO mac- prefix at this level)

config_tree_per_evi._critical_difference: At the OUTER loop-prevention level the timers are prefixed with 'mac-' (mac-restore-timer, mac-restore-max-cycles, mac-reset-restore-cycles-interval). At the INNER local-loop-prevention level the SAME concepts have NO 'mac-' prefix (restore-timer, restore-max-cycles, reset-restore-cycles-interval). Confluence shows them all as 'mac-restore-*' which is WRONG for the LLP sub-tree.

_what_we_tested: network-services evpn instance <I> interface <AC> mac-handling -> 0 keywords
network-services evpn instance <I> interface <AC> mac-handling loop-prevention -> 0 keywords
network-services evpn instance <I> interface <AC> mac-handling local-loop-prevention -> 0 keywords
config_ac_level_NOT_supported_on_this_bu._meaning: On dev_v26_2 (build 8fd38d35a10a) the AC-level mac-handling sub-tree is empty. Loop-prevention is per-EVI only. Test recipes must NOT try to set per-AC LLP timers on this build.

syntax_traps_proven_against_device: show evpn local-loop-prevention -> REJECTED. 'local-loop-prevention' is config-only, not a show keyword.
Outer loop-prevention timers: mac-restore-timer / mac-restore-max-cycles / mac-reset-restore-cycles-interval
Inner local-loop-prevention timers: restore-timer / restore-max-cycles / reset-restore-cycles-interval (NO mac- prefix at LLP level)
ip-loop-* keywords sit alongside MAC keywords directly under 'loop-prevention' (NOT under a separate ip-loop-prevention sub-tree).
ip-loop-action exists; plain 'action' is the MAC-side action keyword (suppress|blackhole|shutdown).
Per-AC mac-handling tree is empty on dev_v26_2 -- LLP is per-EVI only on this build.
When you see 'mac-suppression' / 'mac-history' / 'restore-cycles' in evpn-mac-mobility.json, those are CLEAR commands, not SHOW commands.

discovery_provenance.method: SSH via DNOSSession; ?-completion walk + send_command for each candidate; record valid/invalid via lib.cache_store.CacheStore
